messages:
alex: Heads-up — eu-west1 GPU pool showing a burst of preempt evictions starting ~00:12 UTC. Noticing a pattern: several racks under maintenance so node counts dropped, scheduler started spilling small 1-GPU pods across nodes and increasing fragmentation.
marta: Yep, I spotted 4 training pods got evicted and restarted on different nodes, total fragmentation metric jumped to 0.78. Pod startup queues backed up for about 2min.
praveen: Any scheduler errors in the logs? I want to rule out the new binpack heuristic causing oscillations.
kim: saw a couple of warnings from the binpack plugin: "preferredAffinity conflict" and some soft preempt messages around the same time. Also kube-scheduler repro shows a surge in scoring updates.
sre-bot: :warning: Alert: cluster/eu-west1-gpu-pool fragmentation_high (0.78) at 1777000015 - affected pods: 6 - evictions: 4
alex: Quick root-cause theory: rack maintenance triggers node drains -> small GPU workloads get rebalanced -> binpack puts 1-GPU pods on many nodes to avoid preemption, which increases free-slot fragmentation for big jobs (2+ GPUs). When dedicated training jobs request contiguous slots, they either wait or force preempt smaller pods.
marta: We should avoid mass eviction of long-running training jobs. Proposal: temporarily relax strict binpack for 30m and favor fewer placement hops, even if it means slightly higher per-pod cross-node utilization.
praveen: I can push a quick scheduler config change: reduce binpack scoring weight from 0.9 -> 0.6 and increase co-location score. But that may increase inter-node comm for inference pods.
kim: Tradeoffs: higher co-location reduces fragmentation but increases risk of noisy-neighbor on a single host. Also cost impact: might increase tail latency for small latency-sensitive inference. Can we scope change to label selector workload=training?
alex: Yes, use node affinity/taint trick: add toleration/anti-evict label for pods with annotation redwood/prevent-evict=training; scheduler scoring change can be conditional on pod label. Less blast radius.
marta: Also schedule a descheduler run after the maintenance window to consolidate or drain the tiny spread pods back into compact nodes. That mitigates long-term fragmentation.
praveen: Agreed. Plan: (1) Push conditional binpack weight change for pods labeled training (2) apply label to active training pods via k8s-job controller for the next 24h (3) run descheduler + compacting job 1h after maintenance completes.
kim: I'll run a quick cost estimate: if we co-locate more, short-term egress/interconnect could rise ~8-12% on affected racks. Over 24h that's ~+$700 for eu-west1 pool. Acceptable for stability?
alex: Fine by me for a one-off. We should also bump dedicated autoscaler buffer by +1 node for the next 6h to reduce immediate pressure and avoid further preempts.
marta: Can someone add a note to the incident timeline? And tag infra-oncall.
praveen: Opening a tiny runbook now with commands and rollback:```
# apply conditional config
kubectl apply -f scheduler-config-train-prefer.yaml
# label active jobs
kubectl label pods -l job=training redwood/prevent-evict=training --overwrite
# schedule descheduler job
kubectl apply -f descheduler-compact-after-maint.yaml
```
kim: Thx. I'll monitor metrics and post if anything spikes. If we see >3 evictions in next 30m we revert.
sre-bot: Deploy triggered by @praveen: configmap/scheduler-config -> v2.7.9 (canary) at 1777000150
alex: Rolling back if fragmentation doesn't drop in 20m. Otherwise keep change and follow descheduler plan. :thumbsup:
marta: Noted. I'll check with oncall about the rack maintenance ETA and update the channel.
praveen: Done, runbook created and posted to the incident doc.
kim: Monitoring shows fragmentation dropping to 0.53 after the config change (t=1777000300). Looks promising.
praveen: Great, we'll keep the conditional rule for 6h and then remove it once descheduler compacts.
alex: Thanks team — nice quick coordination.
praveen: closing loop, tagging this as low-sev infra mitigation.
